intent: new painting; portrait style references and old-map layout reference only
prompt:
Create a NEW richly painted manuscript map for a literary print-and-play board based on Shota Rustaveli's The Knight in the Panther's Skin.

REFERENCES: Reference 1 (Tariel) and Reference 2 (Nestan) are STYLE references only: match their accomplished hand-painted tempera/gouache, fine ink contours, convincingly modeled detail, muted mineral pigments, petrol-blue, forest green, warm ochre, parchment and burnished antique gold. Reference 3 is ONLY a rough SPATIAL LAYOUT guide for seven locations and coastline. Completely replace its primitive geometric buildings, trees and mountains with sophisticated detailed painting. Do not copy its symbols, typography, route lines, title, empty rectangular legend, or flat vector look.

OUTPUT: A single seamless flat rectangular map illustration, viewed from above with elevated oblique manuscript landmarks, landscape aspect ratio 592:420 (about 1.4095:1). Request native 3360 x 2384 pixels or highest supported native resolution at that ratio. The canvas itself is the artwork, not a photograph of a sheet, mockup, tabletop, book, or folded object. Opaque background. No writing or text anywhere; all Georgian type will be typeset afterward. No letters, numbers, place names, compass directions, pseudo-calligraphy, watermarks, labels, banners with lettering, UI panels, grids, fold lines, dotted route lines, icons, isolated medallions, or portraits.

SUBJECT: Exactly seven clearly distinguishable principal places in one continuous imaginative story-world, with intricate landscapes, craggy ridges, forest groves, small fields, footpaths, richly painted shorelines, deep mineral-blue sea and delicately painted sailing vessels. Regional styling is an artistic Caucasian and Eastern manuscript interpretation, not a real-world political map. Beautiful and inviting, dignified, detailed, with fine brushwork at print scale. Avoid a generic cartoon fantasy board or repeated clip-art castles.

PLACEMENT, matching reference 3 approximately:
1. ARABIA: upper-left, principal city centered around 13% width, 26% down from top. A graceful warm sandstone court with courtyards, distinct domed halls, gardens, colonnades and slender watchtowers, painted as a substantial inhabited royal city.
2. WILDERNESS/CAVE: upper middle-left, around 37% width, 26% down. A dramatic rocky wooded wilderness with a deep cave mouth, layered cliffs, scattered cypresses and a winding trail. No palace here, no giant literal panther or people.
3. KHATAETI: high upper middle-right around 63% width, 15% down. A rugged mountain stronghold and a modest walled town with earthy red-brown roofs, distinctly different from the royal cities.
4. INDIA: upper-right around 87% width, 26% down. An expansive, ornate golden-ochre royal complex with pillared courtyards, terraces, lush gardens and finely modeled pavilions above a bay; unique architecture rather than a copy of Arabia.
5. MULGHAZANZAR: lower middle-left around 37% width, 63% down. A beautiful compact coastal kingdom, a sea-facing citadel, harbor walls, houses on terraces and a small sheltered inlet, in muted green-blue and pale stone.
6. GULANSHARO: lower middle-right around 63% width, 63% down. A prosperous dense merchant port with varied warehouse roofs, waterfront streets, jetties, gardens, painted merchant ships and an elegant urban skyline. It should read as a trading city, not another fort.
7. KADJETI: lower-right around 87% width, 62% down. An imposing three-gated fortress on a precipitous rocky outcrop, visibly three separate front gateways, tall stone towers and steep surrounding cliffs, muted charcoal-violet stone. Strong and foreboding without monsters, dragons or magical spectacle.

COMPOSITION AND USABILITY: A pale parchment mainland spans the upper half, a richly painted blue sea and large bay occupy the lower-left and middle, Mulghazanzar sits on a western coastal peninsula, Gulansharo on the opposing coast, and Kadjeti lies inland to its east. Coastlines and passages remain roughly like reference 3 but become organic and painterly. The sea passage from Mulghazanzar toward Kadjeti remains visually possible along the lower waters before a land approach. Do not assert modern borders or modern geography.

Reserve naturally quiet pale parchment areas, NOT drawn white boxes, beneath each main landmark for future Georgian names: centered at x13/y39%, x37/y39%, x63/y29%, x87/y39%, x37/y77%, x63/y77%, x87/y82%. Keep the main landmarks above those fields. Leave a quiet parchment title area in the upper-left from x4–24%, y3–13%, and a subdued uncluttered parchment/sea area in lower-left x3–22%, y59–87% for a small route key to be added later. These quiet areas should feel organically part of an illuminated map, not a UI layout.

Finish with a restrained rectangular antique-gold illuminated vine border, echoing the references' exquisite gold rims, with tiny botanical corner flourishes. Preserve a luminous ivory balance and rich selective details rather than dark all-over texture. This must feel like an artisan painted literary map worthy of the detailed character portraits, not a schematic.
